newsitem.title: CHINA: Hyundai Motor seeking China car stake.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor seeking China car stake.

text.p: South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor Co has applied to Chinese authorities for a 22 percent stake in the Sino-French Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile joint venture, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Peugeot Automobiles said last week it had not decided to quit the joint venture, which French newspapers have reported to be on the brink of failure.
Peugeot owns a 30 percent in the venture, which stopped producing cars several months ago. The group's Citroen division runs a joint venture plant in China's central city of Wuhan.

The newspaper Le Monde said Hyundai, Opel and Bayerische Motoren Werke AG were lined up to take Peugeot's place in Guangzhou, capital of southern Guangdong province, if the French carmaker abandoned its project there.

China Daily Business Weekly gave no details of Peugeot's plans for the Guangzhou plant, but said Hyundai's application for a stake had heated up competition among rivals Honda Motor Co, Ford Motor Co and BMW.
